completed_subtasks.subtask: Analyze the proposed HTML structure (or create a preliminary version if Architect is not finished) and design the JavaScript logic for the Tic-Tac-Toe game in 'script.js'. This should include functions for: handling player turns (X and O), detecting clicks on game squares, updating the game board state, checking for win conditions (rows, columns, diagonals), and detecting a draw (all squares filled without a winner). Consider how to represent the board state and communicate it effectively to the UI (handled by Architect or a subsequent task). Start implementing the core logic.

Create the basic file structure for the Tic-Tac-Toe project in the current directory, including 'index.html', 'style.css', and 'script.js'. Link the CSS and JS files in the 'index.html' file and set up a basic, professional-looking HTML grid for the game board (e.g., using a table or divs). Ensure appropriate IDs are used for game squares to be accessed by scripts.

Continue with implementing the JavaScript logic. Since the structural files are being created by Architect, you can finalize the core game loop, win detection, and draw conditions. You can also begin integrating basic logging or temporary UI updates if needed, in anticipation of the Architect's files.

Now that you've set up the basic HTML structure, style the game using 'style.css' to make it look professional, clean, and modern. Add visual separation between squares. Consider how to highlight the winning combination of squares when the game ends. Maintain responsiveness if possible. You can use some dummy 'X' and 'O' placeholders in the HTML to test your styling, but make sure the base state (empty) looks good. Wait for LogicDev to provide the structure needed for real 'X' and 'O' rendering later.

Refine the logic within 'script.js'. Start by accessing the DOM elements created by the Architect. Implement click event listeners for the game squares that invoke the turn-handling logic. Integrate the UI update functions (which will eventually interact with the visual design) so that the game state changes are reflected in the HTML. Finish the core game logic by implementing the win-condition and draw-detection checks against the live board state.

With the JavaScript logic complete, update 'style.css' and potentially add basic visual transitions for a polished look. Crucially, coordinate with the previous 'script.js' developer (if possible, or infer from standard patterns) to implement styling for the winning square combinations. For example, if 'script.js' adds a class like '.winner' to the relevant squares, define that class in 'style.css' to provide visual feedback. Ensure the final look is professional and cohesive.

Finalize the 'script.js' file by integrating the logic with the DOM structure created by the Architect. Ensure click event listeners are correctly attached to the game cells, player turns alternate (X and O), the board state updates correctly, win/draw conditions are accurately detected and displayed (potentially highlighting winning cells based on the Architect's styling), and add a functional 'Restart Game' button that resets the state and the UI. Perform basic testing.
